entities.name: Alagille syndrome
observations: Human ALGS liver shows hepatic cholesterol accumulation with altered cholesterol-regulatory gene expression and reduced CYP7A1 mRNA.
The canonical FXR–FGF19–CYP7A1 defect is not directly established in human ALGS; FGF19 production and FGFR4/β-Klotho signaling were not directly measured.

entities.name: ALGS cholesterol feedback
observations: In a direct human case-control study, 23 ALGS patients were assessed and liver tissue from 5 patients showed increased hepatic cholesterol, increased LDLR, SR-BI, HMGCR, and ABCG transporter expression, reduced CYP7A1 mRNA, and failure to suppress mature SREBP2.
These findings support impaired hepatic sterol negative feedback and cholesterol accumulation in ALGS.

entities.name: ALGS bile acid conversion
observations: ALGS liver showed reduced CYP7A1, the rate-limiting enzyme of classical cholesterol-to-bile-acid synthesis, while hepatic cholesterol and bile-acid contents were increased and correlated.
This supports abnormal cholesterol-to-bile-acid conversion or handling with cholestatic retention rather than accelerated CYP7A1-mediated synthesis.

entities.name: ALGS FXR FGF19 axis
observations: Human ALGS evidence is insufficient to conclude that the canonical FXR–FGF19–CYP7A1 axis is intrinsically defective.

The ALGS study found increased SHP mRNA but did not directly assess FGF19 production, FGFR4/β-Klotho signaling, or pathway responsiveness; human hepatocyte evidence supports both FGF19-dependent and SHP-mediated feedback.

entities.name: Traumatic CSF rhinorrhea
observations: Salty postnasal drainage after blunt head trauma is a classic clue to cerebrospinal-fluid leakage through the nose.
The combination of epistaxis and bilateral hemotympanum indicates a skull-base fracture pattern; nasal CSF leakage most often reflects an anterior skull-base defect.

entities.name: Basilar skull fracture
observations: Blunt head trauma with bilateral hemotympanum and epistaxis is strongly suggestive of basilar skull injury.
Temporal-bone or middle-cranial-fossa involvement can produce hemotympanum, while anterior skull-base involvement can produce CSF rhinorrhea.

entities.name: Salty postnasal drainage
observations: In this trauma context, new salty drainage is more specific for CSF rhinorrhea than for anosmia, recurrent epistaxis, or orbital-floor fracture.
